title: Thermal One-point Functions and Asymptotic CFT Data: QFT in AdS
authors: Ilija Burić, Francesco Mangialardi, Francesco Russo, Volker Schomerus, Alessandro Vichi
abstract: We investigate the thermal partition and one-point functions of the three-dimensional conformal field theory dual to a massive interacting scalar field in AdS$_4$. Using thermal inversion formulas, we determine the asymptotic behaviour of the spectral density and OPE coefficients involving heavy operators at fixed spin. We first analyse these CFT data for the generalised free field, corresponding to the non-interacting bulk theory. Then we compute the first-order perturbative corrections induced by the cubic and quartic bulk interactions. The thermal observables considered here probe a sector associated with operators of large dimension and, in the bulk description, a regime dominated by states with large particle number. This regime remains comparatively unexplored even in generalised free field theory. Remarkably, the asymptotic formulas obtained from thermal inversion remain quantitatively accurate far from the asymptotic regime, describing CFT data reliably already at intermediate conformal weights. Our results show that this feature survives the inclusion of bulk interactions and provide new analytic control over heavy-state data in conformal field theories.
summary: This work analyzes thermal properties of a 3D CFT dual to an interacting scalar field in AdS4. Using advanced techniques like thermal inversion formulas, the authors determine the asymptotic behavior of key observables such as spectral densities and OPE coefficients. The main achievement is demonstrating that these derived asymptotic results maintain high quantitative accuracy even when considering intermediate energy regimes and weak interactions.
main_problem: The research investigates thermal partition functions and one-point functions of a 3D CFT dual to a massive scalar field in AdS4.
main_result: The authors derive asymptotic formulas for spectral density and OPE coefficients that remain quantitatively accurate even at intermediate conformal weights, surviving the inclusion of bulk interactions.
method: They employ thermal inversion formulas applied to correlation functions derived from analyzing the partition function using techniques involving conformal block decompositions and high-temperature expansions.
model_or_system: The system is a Conformal Field Theory (CFT) in 3D, holographically dual to a massive interacting scalar field theory ($\Phi^3, \Phi^4$) propagating in Anti-de Sitter space (AdS$_4$).
key_observables: Thermal partition function, one-point functions of primary fields, spectral density $ho(\Delta, \ell)$, and OPE coefficients ($\lambda_{\phi O}$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), chemical potential ($\mu$), conformal dimension ($\Delta$), and spin ($\ell$). The analysis focuses on the high-temperature limit ($ eta 	o 0$) and large $\Delta$ regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies fundamentally on the AdS/CFT correspondence, utilizing techniques derived from conformal block expansions and asymptotic analysis in complex variables.
figures_summary: Figures compare asymptotic formulas for spectral density and OPE coefficients against exact results obtained through various limits (e.g., GFF theory).
paper_structure: The paper systematically progresses by first analyzing the non-interacting Generalized Free Field (GFF) theory, then incorporating perturbative corrections from cubic and quartic bulk interactions, applying thermal inversion techniques throughout.
why_interesting: While focused on AdS/CFT, the rigorous development of thermal effective field theories for one-point functions and the extraction of universal asymptotic data are powerful analytical tools applicable to understanding critical phenomena in many quantum systems.
